decisions.reason: Changing Lead Status after LinkedIn connection acceptance does not alter which communication channels are visible in the HubSpot lead record.
The connection-status rule does not change HubSpot list creation or management behavior.
The source establishes a Lead Status value but does not change task-assignment behavior.
The source does not change the reporting deliverable or define any reporting use of the connected status.

Although Lead Status is a classification mechanism, the accepted-connection mapping is already owned by the atomic activity-status requirement and does not necessarily change the candidate's existing classification-mechanism state.
The Lead Status transition does not alter whether lead notes are included.
The source does not state that the connected status triggers or changes any nurturing workflow.
The source concerns a status update following LinkedIn acceptance, not HubSpot-list synchronization to MeetAlfred.
The status rule does not change the data-flow map deliverable or its mapped MeetAlfred-to-HubSpot direction.
Connection acceptance occurs within the LinkedIn context, but the source does not change campaign channel, platform, or automation mode.
The LinkedIn connection-status mapping does not alter the email integration between MeetAlfred and HubSpot.
The word connected describes the lead's status, not whether the MeetAlfred integration must remain connected.
